newsitem.title: USA: Tidewater says won't build but will cut debt.
newsitem.headline: Tidewater says won't build but will cut debt.

text.p: Tidewater Inc said on Monday that it will use its $200 million free cashflow to cut debt rather than build new offshore service vessels.
The company, which will take on $500 million of debt once its acquisition of OIL Ltd of the UK is cleared by regulators said that it expects regulatory approval of the deal by mid-May.

Following an announcement on Friday that Edison Chouest would add 17 new ships to its fleet, Tidewater chairman William O'Malley said the company may delay the repatriation of vessels working overseas to the Gulf of Mexico.

"Tidewater has repatriated to the U.S. Gulf of Mexico eight U.S.-flagged supply vessels from various international markets over the past year and had planned to repatriate an additional six vessels over the next six to 12 months," O'Malley said.

"However, because of the announced plans by a few U.S. Gulf of Mexico competitors to build new vessels and because of the strong demand for supply vessels in the international markets, the company will reevaluate its repatriation of additional vessels to the U.S. market," he added. ((-- David Chance New York Newsroom 212 859 1902))
